notes:
Setting up a new device goes from minutes to seconds: first sync now restores from a snapshot instead of replaying your entire edit history.

**New**

- **Snapshot onboarding (dev).** When you sign in on a new device, the app now downloads a compact, end-to-end-encrypted **snapshot** of your current notes, restores it in one step ("Restoring from snapshot… N of M"), and then syncs only what changed since — instead of replaying every edit you've ever made (~182,000 operations on a mature vault, minutes of waiting) it applies a few thousand, targeting **seconds**. Privacy is unchanged by design: snapshots are built and encrypted **on your own devices** — the server still can't read anything; it just stores one more opaque blob. If anything about a snapshot is off, first sync quietly falls back to the old full-replay path. (PRD Addendum 30 §AA.)
  - Your desktop refreshes the snapshot weekly (and right after an encryption-key rotation); your iPhone pitches in when it's on Wi-Fi and charged, so even mobile-only use keeps a fresh snapshot.
  - Verified end-to-end: a snapshot-restored device is proven **byte-identical** to one that replayed full history, across a torture-test vault (tables, merged journals, deletions, multi-device edits).

**Under the hood**

- The snapshot is a sealed bundle of ordinary sync operations synthesized per supersession lane from materialized state with stored HLC provenance, self-verified against a fresh in-memory apply before sealing, and applied through the standard op-apply path on restore (one SQLite transaction — a failed restore rolls back to a clean slate). Server: three additive endpoints, latest-only retention (the op-log/history is never pruned), stale-publisher 409s. Consume retries once on transient network failures; restore/publish outcomes feed consent-gated telemetry (counts only) + Export Diagnostics. Behind the `snapshot_onboarding` gradual-rollout flag (dev-on) + kill switch, riding the dev-only `sync` gate. (Addendum 30 §AA; PRs #644/#646/#647/#648; sync-sim 86/86 incl. the byte-identical equivalence proof.)
